answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, and slash that stake when an adjudicated fraud claim is upheld. A Sybil operator can still forge many identities, but must fund each one separately and risks losing the capital, so multiplying accounts raises the cost instead of multiplying influence for free. The oasis of cheap registration gives way to a dune of collateral that attackers must cross.
